spans.claim: The body of the victim was never found despite a thorough search
spans.anchor: The body of the woman was not found, and the most rigid and tireless search failed to develop the slightest trace of the corpse
spans.span: The body of the woman was not found, and the most rigid and tireless search failed to develop the slightest trace of the corpse, or the manner of its disposal.

spans.claim: Victor Ancona was arrested at the victim's house with blood on his clothes
spans.anchor: There was also blood on the prisoner's coat and the leg of his trousers, and the heavy Mexican knife was also bloody

spans.claim: The law requires direct proof of death or criminal violence for murder conviction
spans.anchor: It is the fixed and immutable law of this State... that both components of the corpus delicti shall not be established by circumstantial evidence

spans.claim: The judge directs the jury to acquit due to lack of corpus delicti
spans.anchor: I am, therefore, gentlemen of the jury, compelled to direct you to find the prisoner not guilty
spans.span: I am, therefore, gentlemen of the jury, compelled to direct you to find the prisoner not guilty.

spans.claim: The victim threatened to expose the murderer with evidence
spans.anchor: I have all the evidence to convict you of murdering him! The Archbishop will have it to-morrow! They shall hang you!
spans.span: I have all the evidence to convict you of murdering him! The Archbishop will have it to-morrow! They shall hang you! Do you hear me?

spans.claim: The chemical dissolution of the body was performed in the bath-room
spans.anchor: He fastened the tubes to two of the gas jets, put the burners under the tub, turned the gas on full, and lighted it
spans.span: He fastened the tubes to two of the gas jets, put the burners under the tub, turned the gas on full, and lighted it.

spans.claim: Sulfuric acid and nitrate of soda were used to dissolve the body
spans.anchor: He threw into the tub the woman's clothing and the papers... and dropped them carefully into the sulphuric acid

spans.claim: The bath-room was cleaned thoroughly after the dissolution
spans.anchor: He turned off the gas quickly and stepped back out of the room... rinsed the tub clean, and replaced the metal outlet

spans.claim: The disappearance of the body prevents legal punishment despite guilt
spans.anchor: The law of New York compels me to acquit you... You are now at liberty to leave this court-room, not guiltless of the crime of murder, perhaps, but at least rid of its punishment

spans.claim: Randolph Mason is a lawyer who exploits legal loopholes to evade punishment
spans.anchor: He found holes in the law through which his clients escaped, holes that by the profession at large were not suspected to exist
spans.span: He found holes in the law through which his clients escaped, holes that by the profession at large were not suspected to exist, and that frequently astonished the judges.

spans.claim: The victim's dress was covered with blood matching the murder weapon

spans.claim: The police officers heard the victim's cries accusing the murderer
spans.anchor: They heard a woman's voice cry out in great anger: "I know that you love her and that you want to get rid of me..."

spans.claim: The victim was killed before the police broke into the house
spans.anchor: When arrested, Victor Ancona had screamed like a wild beast taken in a trap and sank down

spans.claim: The acid fumes escaped through the open window during the dissolution
spans.anchor: The fumes had escaped through the open window; this he now closed
spans.span: The fumes had escaped through the open window; this he now closed and set himself to putting the bath-room in order, and effectually removing every trace of his night's work.

spans.claim: The legal principle of corpus delicti is central to the case
spans.anchor: The question before your Honor is simple. If the corpus delicti, the body of the crime, has been proven, as required by the laws of the commonwealth, then this case should go to the jury

spans.claim: The victim was last seen alive at her residence
spans.anchor: Nina San Croix had resided for many years in the house in which the prisoner was arrested
spans.span: It had been shown that Nina San Croix had resided for many years in the house in which the prisoner was arrested; that she had lived by herself, with no other companion than an old negro servant; that her past was unknown, and that she received no visitors, save the Mexican sailor, who came to her house at long intervals.

spans.claim: The accused had motive to kill the victim
spans.anchor: Her voice is heard, raised high in the greatest passion, denouncing him, and charging that he is a murderer
spans.span: Her voice is heard, raised high in the greatest passion, denouncing him, and charging that he is a murderer, that she has the evidence and will reveal it, that he shall be hanged, and that he shall not be rid of her.

spans.claim: The victim's body was dismembered and dissolved to prevent discovery
spans.anchor: When he had finally cut the body into as small pieces as possible, he replaced the knife in its sheath, washed his hands
spans.span: When he had finally cut the body into as small pieces as possible, he replaced the knife in its sheath, washed his hands, and went out of the bath-room and down stairs to the lower hall.
